results.note: De triplici habitaculo translated into Middle English during the fifteenth century, along with French, German, Dutch, Castilian, Catalan, Italian, and Portuguese versions (public domain medieval translations).
De unctione capitis et de pedibus lavandis: No English translation found despite searching medieval sermon collections and PL references.
De vanitate saeculi: No specific English translation found in searches, though related medieval Latin vanity-theme works exist.

De visitatione infirmorum: Multiple works with similar titles exist; medieval English version exists in MS. Bodl. 789, and H.E. Sigerist provided translation (1960), but uncertain if it refers to this specific anonymous work.
De vita Christiana: Attributed to Pseudo-Augustinus or Pelagius in medieval manuscripts, but no English translation found.
Expositio cantici Magnificat: No specific English translation found; compilation volumes of medieval Magnificat commentaries exist but not this work alone.
Sententiae miscellaneae: No English translation found in searches of medieval Latin sentence collections.
Soliloquia animae ad Deum: Medieval apocrypha (falsely attributed to Augustine), available in PL XL 863-897, but no English translation found in searches.
Speculum peccatoris: Widespread medieval devotional text with English translation dated 1593 (per Online Books Page), widely translated into English, German, and French during the late Middle Ages.

Speculum: Likely refers to one of several medieval Speculum works (Speculum Humanae Salvationis, Speculum Inclusorum) which have Middle English and early English translations, but unclear which specific work.
Ad fratres in eremo commorantes: Pseudo-Augustinian sermon collection (Sermones ad fratres in eremo) well-attested in medieval manuscripts, but no English translation found.
De miraculis S. Stephani: Cataloged in Digital Latin Library, attributed to anonymous author, no English translation found.
De unitate sanctae Trinitatis: No specific English translation found despite searches for medieval Trinity treatises.
Sermo Arianorum: Fourth-century text; Augustine wrote Contra sermonem arianorum against it, but no English translation of the sermon itself found.
Contra Fulgentium: Possibly the Libellus aduersus Fulgentium Donatistam, early Christian theological work, but no English translation found.
De praedestinatione Dei: Small work on divine predestination (1156 words), no English translation found in searches of medieval predestination literature.
De praedestinatione et gratia: Appears in PL 45 and 65; no specific English translation found despite searches for medieval predestination-and-grace works.
Regula S. Pachomii: Jerome's Latin translation available; English translations include Schodde's from the Ethiopic (PDFs available online), and Fr. Lawrence of Jordanville version (public domain).
Admonitio ad virgines: Related work Admonitio ad filium spiritualem has partial Old English translation by Ælfric, but no English translation of this specific work found.
Commentarii in Genesim: Large biblical commentary (86,441 words) in PL 50 cols 893B-1048B; no English translation found despite searches for medieval Genesis commentaries.
Commentarii in libros Regum: Large biblical commentary (88,087 words) in PL 50; no English translation found in searches of medieval biblical commentaries.
Epistola: Generic title appearing in multiple PL volumes (50, 89, 96), likely fragmentary correspondence; no specific English translation found.
Epitaphium Hilarii: Brief epitaphic text (98 words); searches found Venantius Fortunatus's vita of Saint Hilary but not this specific epitaph translation.

Sententia ad monachos: Similar title exists for Evagrius Ponticus (with Jeremy Driscoll English translation in ACW 59), but batch entry is by Auctor incertus, likely a different work; no translation found.
Sententiae piam interpretationem desiderantes: Appears in PL 50 cols 361A-368C (3534 words); no English translation found.

De promissionibus et praedictionibus Dei: Large work on divine promises/predictions (47,933 words) in PL 51 cols 733-858A; variously attributed to Quodvultdeus or Prosper; no English translation found.
Carmina: Poems appearing across PL volumes 53, 87, 155 (2,214 words total); no English translation found for this anonymous collection.
Praedestinatus: First English translation published by Brepols Library of Christian Sources (bilingual edition, vol. 6), edited by Guido Stucco, ISBN 9782503596761; modern copyrighted translation.
Vita S. Maximi Taurinensis: Biography of Saint Maximus of Turin (11,922 words); searches found English translation of his sermons (B. Ramsey, ACW 50) but not this specific vita translation.
Coronis Sidoniana: Related to Sidonius Apollinaris tradition (1,135 words), but no English translation found despite searches on Sidonius and medieval coronae/wreaths literature.
Epitaphium: Generic title for epitaphs across multiple PL volumes (58, 59, 72, 98, 131, 154, 166); likely multiple different epitaphs, no translations found.
Appendix III: Fragment in PL 59 cols 157A-190D (11,004 words), likely miscellaneous appendix material; no English translation found.
De computo paschali: Easter computation treatise (5,939 words); searches found Bede's De computo with translations but not this anonymous work.
De genealogiis patriarcharum: Biblical genealogy treatise (9,600 words) in PL 59 cols 523A-546A; no English translation found.
Ordo monasticus: Brief monastic order text (1,357 words) in PL 59; no English translation found despite searches of monastic rule collections.
Fragmentum alterius vitae: Fragment of a biography/life (707 words) in PL 62 cols 47C-50A; no English translation found.
Notitia: Generic title (appears in PL 62, 69, 89); likely biographical notices or registers; no English translation found.
Commentarius in librum De consolatione philosophiae: Commentary on Boethius (4,117 words) in PL 64 cols 1239A-1246D; Latin text on Wikisource but no English translation found.
Alia regula: Another monastic rule (551 words) in PL 66; no English translation found in searches of medieval monastic rule collections.

Ordo Romanus: Medieval Roman liturgical order; English translations exist: E.G. Cuthbert Atchley (1905), and Alan Griffiths contemporary translation running parallel to Latin text (public domain and modern versions available).
Regula Tarnatensis: Sixth-century monastic rule based on Augustine; described in secondary literature but no English translation found.
Regula consensoria monachorum: Appears in Barlow's Iberian Fathers with English translation as 'Monastic Agreement'; also referenced as having English versions in monastic studies literature.

Regula cujusdam patris: Anonymous monastic rule (2,652 words) in PL 66; academic translation with commentary exists (Academia.edu reference found), but unclear if this is an English translation or only Latin scholarly edition.
De inventione capitis Joannis Baptistae: Account of the finding of John the Baptist's head (15,174 words), attested in medieval manuscripts and legendary literature; no English translation found.
Collectio II decretorum pontificum Romanorum: Collection of papal decrees (12,080 words) in PL 67 cols 315-346B; no specific English translation of this collection found.
